slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
Anjou is famous for Chenin Blanc, but its Cabernet Franc is equally impressive. From the entry-level Anjou Rouge to the select Anjou-Villages, up to the pinnacle Anjou-Brissac, and the crowning glory of Saumur-Champigny — these five AOCs form the complete spectrum of Anjou-Saumur reds.

Learning Objectives

🍷 Master the Anjou Red AOC Hierarchy

Quality differences and regulations for Anjou, Anjou-Villages, and Anjou-Brissac

🏰 Understand Saumur-Champigny

Cabernet Franc on tuffeau — why it is called the most elegant red in the Loire
slides.1.title: Anjou Rouge — Introduction to Anjou Reds
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Anjou Rouge
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Dominated by Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon, small amounts of Gamay permitted; light to medium body
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Anjou-Villages
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Strictly limited to Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon; higher quality, mainly from schist-soil villages
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Anjou-Brissac
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The premier village of Anjou-Villages, located in Brissac-Quincé; mixed schist and sandstone soils give better structure
slides.1.content:
The three tiers of Anjou reds represent different levels of quality aspiration:

Anjou Rouge: Everyday drinking, flexible blends, fresh fruit, best enjoyed young.

Anjou-Villages: Selected villages, pure Cabernet, more mineral and with ageing potential.

Anjou-Brissac: Top-tier expression — the unique schist slopes of Brissac deliver complexity with spicy character.
slides.2.title: Saumur Rouge and Saumur-Champigny
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Saumur Rouge
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Saumur's entry-level red; tuffeau soils; light and elegant; Cabernet Franc dominant
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Saumur-Champigny
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Saumur's finest red wine appellation; ancient tuffeau plateau; Cabernet Franc shows red-fruit florals and silky tannins
slides.2.content:
Saumur-Champigny is the king of reds in Anjou-Saumur. This small appellation sits southeast of Saumur on an ancient tuffeau plateau.

Typical style: fresh raspberry, strawberry, and violet aromas; silky tannins; crisp acidity; a subtle mineral quality from the tuffeau.

The best vintages can age 10–15 years, developing leather, tobacco, and spice complexity. Legendary producer: Clos Rougeard — one of the Loire's most iconic reds.
slides.3.title: Quiz
slides.3.questions.0.question: What is the primary grape variety of Saumur-Champigny?
slides.3.questions.0.explanation: Saumur-Champigny is dominated by Cabernet Franc; the tuffeau soils lend a distinctive lightness and elegance that sets it apart.
